THE PEOPLE BEHIND THE NEED

About Us

Clearer communication between EMS and hospitals, so care teams can focus on the people who need them.

Hospital Connect is a project exploring how EMS dispatchers, paramedics and receiving hospitals can coordinate resource requests more clearly, with a focus on British Columbia and the pressures faced by rural communities.

Our aim is simple: make it easier to send a request, see which hospital accepts, and keep the receiving destination visible to the EMS team.

A FIRST-HAND PERSPECTIVE

What a BC paramedic shared

WY

William Yeung

Paramedic in British Columbia

In the account recorded in our supplied project notes, William describes the work from dispatch and patient transport through to hospital triage and handoff. His central concern is transferring care so paramedics can return to emergencies in the community.

Source: AI Hacathon (1).pdf, section 4, supplied by the project team. The themes below are paraphrased from that account, not direct quotations or independently verified findings about every BC facility.

01

Not knowing capacity before arrival

William describes limited visibility into hospital beds, trauma-team availability and real-time capacity for paramedics and computer-aided dispatch. Teams may only discover what is available when they arrive.

02

Long transfers extending long shifts

He reports that rural ER closures can force longer-distance transfers, extending a standard 12-hour shift by another 3–6 hours and increasing pressure around driving limits.

03

Waiting to hand over care

His account describes waits of 1–2 hours before triage assessment begins, with paramedics spending additional time holding patients in hospital hallways rather than returning to community calls.

04

Updates that are hard to read on the road

Driving and hands-on patient care can prevent crews from reading computer-aided dispatch text alerts during transport. William highlights the resulting information lag during important transport decisions.

05

Information spread across separate systems

William describes separate regional hospital IT networks and a gap between interfacility transfer coordination and the real-time ER information emergency dispatch needs.

WHY WE ARE BUILDING

Make the next step clearer

This account helps explain why communication matters alongside resources and staffing. We are exploring a focused coordination workflow: EMS sends a resource request, a hospital accepts, and EMS sees the accepting hospital.

Whether that workflow reduces delays in practice still needs to be tested with healthcare teams.

Where the project stands

The current app is a shared public prototype using invented hospital locations and capacity. It does not provide verified live capacity, clinical decisions or emergency dispatch. Do not enter real patient information.

William’s account provides context for the problem; it is not presented as an endorsement of the app.
